glossary.definition: The rules, processes, and controls an organization uses to keep cloud resources aligned with business, security, cost, and compliance requirements.
A key-value metadata label used to organize and report on Azure resources.
A governance service that evaluates resources and actions against organizational rules and can audit or enforce compliance.
A control-plane protection that blocks deletion or modification of a protected Azure scope or resource.
Infrastructure as code: defining infrastructure in machine-readable files so deployment is repeatable and automatable.
Azure Resource Manager: Azure's common management and deployment layer for resources.
Operational data emitted by systems, such as metrics, logs, traces, events, and application measurements.
Kusto Query Language: the query language used to analyze log data in Azure Monitor Log Analytics.
JavaScript Object Notation: a text format for structured data. ARM templates can be written as JSON documents.

authoring_notes: Scope authority: the Microsoft AZ-900 study guide, skills measured as of July 20, 2026. The scalar 0.325 is the midpoint of Microsoft's published 30–35% range and is planning metadata rather than an exact per-exam percentage. Task and skill IDs are internal stable IDs following the current Microsoft heading/bullet order, not Microsoft-published numbering. The current exam guide is narrower than some adjacent Microsoft Learn modules; extra topics such as the Service Trust Portal and cost-optimization subtopics are not expanded unless they directly support one of the current guide bullets. prompts.label: WHY CAN THE SAME DESIGN COST DIFFERENT AMOUNTS?

reveal.text: Azure cost depends on several variables. Important factors include the selected service and size, how much you use it, the region, chargeable data transfer, and the pricing or purchasing option.

items: Resource type, service tier, size, and quantity
Usage duration or transactions
Azure region
Outbound or cross-boundary data transfer where charges apply
Pricing option, commitment, licensing, or discounts that apply to the workload

reveal.text: Do not assume 'the cloud' has one fixed price. Cost is driven by the selected service plus actual usage and commercial configuration.

reveal.text: The Azure Pricing Calculator is a web tool for estimating the cost of a planned Azure solution before or while you design it. You select services and expected usage to build an estimate.
Use the calculator for planning and comparing expected costs before deployment. It is an estimate, not the source for analyzing charges that have already occurred.
Pricing Calculator estimates future or proposed usage. Microsoft Cost Management helps analyze and control actual and forecast cloud spending.

reveal.text: Microsoft Cost Management provides tools to analyze Azure costs, monitor spending patterns, create budgets, and help organizations control cloud spend.

items: Analyze charges by dimensions such as subscription, resource, service, or tag.
Create budgets and alerts to track spending against a target.
Review trends and forecasts to understand where cost is going.

reveal.text: Existing spend, budgets, cost analysis, and spend trends point to Cost Management rather than the Pricing Calculator.

reveal.text: An Azure tag is a key-value metadata label applied to supported Azure resources, resource groups, and some other scopes. Tags help organize resources and can make cost and ownership reporting easier.
Use consistent tags such as environment, costCenter, application, or owner when teams need to filter, group, inventory, or report on resources across technical boundaries.
A tag describes a resource; it does not grant permissions. Use Azure RBAC for authorization and Azure Policy when rules must enforce or audit resource configuration.

reveal.text: Microsoft Purview provides data governance, data-security, and compliance capabilities that help organizations understand, govern, and protect data across their data estate.
Use Purview when the problem is discovering or governing data, understanding where sensitive data exists, or supporting data-related compliance and risk-management processes.
Purview focuses on data governance, security, and compliance. Azure Policy evaluates Azure resource configuration and can enforce organizational standards on resource state.

reveal.text: Azure Policy evaluates Azure resources and actions against organizational rules. Policy can audit noncompliant resources, deny certain changes, or use other effects to help enforce standards at scale.
Use Azure Policy when a rule must apply consistently. Examples include allowing only approved regions, requiring certain tags, or checking that resources meet a required configuration.
Azure RBAC asks: who is allowed to perform this action at this scope? Azure Policy asks: does the resource or action comply with the organization's rule? Both can apply to the same request.

reveal.text: A resource lock protects Azure control-plane resources from accidental deletion or modification even when a user otherwise has permission. Locks can be applied at subscription, resource-group, or resource scope.

cells.effect: Authorized users can read and modify the resource but cannot delete it through the protected control plane.
Authorized users can read the resource but cannot update or delete it through the protected control plane.

reveal.text: A lock is an extra protection against control-plane changes; it is not a replacement for RBAC. Also, a resource lock does not automatically protect data-plane data inside a service.

nodes.title: Tags, Policy, locks, and RBAC solve different problems

reveal.text: Tags are metadata labels, Azure Policy evaluates resource compliance, resource locks block specified control-plane changes, and Azure RBAC grants management permissions. They often work together, but they solve different governance problems.

cells.question: How should I label and organize this resource?
Does this resource/configuration comply with the rule?
Should deletion or modification be blocked even for authorized users?
Who may perform which management actions at this scope?

reveal.text: Tags describe. Policy governs configuration. Locks protect against destructive control-plane changes. RBAC authorizes people and identities.
Label or group → tag. Enforce or audit a standard → Policy. Prevent deletion → lock. Grant permission → RBAC.

reveal.text: The Azure portal is a browser-based graphical interface for creating, configuring, and monitoring Azure resources and services.
Use the portal when a human needs an interactive visual interface, especially for exploration, learning, one-off configuration, or viewing dashboards.
The portal is convenient for interactive work, but repeatable deployments are usually better expressed with command-line automation or infrastructure as code.

nodes.title: Cloud Shell, Azure CLI, and Azure PowerShell

reveal.text: Azure Cloud Shell is a browser-accessible shell environment for managing Azure. It provides command-line tools including Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell without requiring you to install those tools on the computer you are using.

cells.style: Cross-platform command-line interface using az commands, convenient for shell scripts.
PowerShell modules and cmdlets, convenient for PowerShell automation and object pipelines.
Hosted shell where you can run Azure CLI or Azure PowerShell from a browser.

reveal.text: Cloud Shell is the hosted environment. Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell are management toolsets you can run in Cloud Shell or from your own configured machine.

reveal.text: Azure Arc extends Azure management and governance capabilities to supported resources outside Azure, including on-premises and other-cloud environments.
Use Azure Arc when selected non-Azure infrastructure should appear in Azure management. Supported Azure governance, inventory, and operations capabilities can then extend across hybrid environments.

prompts.label: ARC DOES NOT MOVE THE RESOURCE

reveal.text: Azure Arc connects supported external resources to Azure management. It does not mean the workload has been migrated into an Azure datacenter.

reveal.text: Infrastructure as code (IaC) defines infrastructure in machine-readable files. This makes environments repeatable and automatable instead of relying only on manual clicks.

items: Repeat the same deployment more consistently.
Review and version configuration changes like other code.
Reduce manual configuration drift and setup mistakes.
Recreate environments from a declared configuration.

prompts.label: IAC IS A PRACTICE, NOT ONE AZURE SERVICE

reveal.text: IaC is the approach. Azure Resource Manager templates are one Azure-native way to describe infrastructure declaratively.

reveal.text: Azure Resource Manager (ARM) is Azure's management and deployment layer. Tools such as the portal, Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell, and templates send management requests through ARM.

items: Management tool or template sends a request
Azure Resource Manager authenticates and authorizes the request
ARM sends the operation to the appropriate Azure resource provider
Azure returns the resulting resource state

reveal.text: If the question asks about Azure's common control plane for deploying and managing resources, think Azure Resource Manager.

reveal.text: An ARM template is a declarative JSON file that describes Azure resources and their desired configuration. Azure Resource Manager uses the template to deploy those resources in a repeatable way.

prompts.label: READ THE SHAPE OF A TEMPLATE

annotations.title: Schema
annotations.explanation: The schema identifies the template language structure.

annotations.title: Resources
annotations.explanation: The resources array declares Azure resources that ARM should deploy.

annotations.title: Resource type
annotations.explanation: The type tells ARM which resource provider and resource type to create.

annotations.title: Expression
annotations.explanation: ARM template expressions can derive values, such as using the current resource group's location.

reveal.text: A template states the desired resources and configuration. It is not a recording of portal clicks or a list of manual setup steps.

reveal.text: Azure Advisor analyzes supported Azure resources and provides personalized recommendations to improve areas such as reliability, security, performance, cost, and operational excellence.
Use Advisor when you want recommendations for improving an existing Azure environment based on Microsoft best practices and information about your deployed resources.
Advisor recommends improvements. Azure Monitor collects and analyzes operational telemetry so you can observe what systems are doing.

reveal.text: Azure Service Health reports Azure service incidents, planned maintenance, and health advisories. The information is personalized to services and regions relevant to your Azure environment.
Use Service Health when you need to know whether an Azure platform issue or planned maintenance may be affecting your subscriptions or deployed services.
Service Health reports Azure platform events relevant to you. It does not replace application telemetry, metrics, logs, or tracing collected with Azure Monitor.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-900: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals — skills measured as of July 20, 2026
Describe monitoring tools in Azure — Microsoft Learn

reveal.text: Azure Monitor is Azure's monitoring platform for collecting, analyzing, and acting on telemetry from applications, infrastructure, and Azure services.

items: Metrics: numeric time-series measurements.
Logs: event and record data that can be queried.
Application telemetry: requests, dependencies, exceptions, and performance data through Application Insights.
Alerts: rules that detect conditions and trigger notifications or automated actions.

reveal.text: When you need to collect, analyze, visualize, or alert on operational data, think Azure Monitor. It is the umbrella monitoring service for Azure resources and applications.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-900: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals — skills measured as of July 20, 2026
Describe monitoring tools in Azure — Microsoft Learn

reveal.text: Log Analytics is the Azure Monitor experience for querying and analyzing log data stored in a Log Analytics workspace. Queries use Kusto Query Language (KQL).
Use Log Analytics when you need to search, correlate, aggregate, or investigate log records across monitored resources.
Logs contain detailed records that are queried as data. Metrics are numeric time-series values optimized for measuring changing quantities such as CPU percentage or request count.

prompts.label: WHAT IS AN AZURE MONITOR ALERT?

reveal.text: An Azure Monitor alert watches telemetry or resource conditions and becomes active when an authored rule is met. Alerts can notify people or trigger actions through action groups.

items: Collect a signal such as a metric or log result
Evaluate the alert rule condition
Fire the alert when the condition is met
Use an action group for notification or automation

reveal.text: If the requirement says 'notify me when this metric or log condition crosses a threshold,' the key feature is an Azure Monitor alert.

reveal.text: Application Insights is an Azure Monitor capability for application performance monitoring. It helps developers observe application requests, dependencies, failures, performance, and related telemetry.
Use Application Insights to understand how an application behaves from the inside. Examples include slow requests, failed dependencies, exceptions, and end-to-end request performance.
Application Insights observes your application. Service Health tells you about Azure platform incidents, planned maintenance, and advisories that may affect services you use.

nodes.title: Advisor, Service Health, and Azure Monitor

reveal.text: Azure Advisor recommends improvements, Azure Service Health reports Azure platform events relevant to you, and Azure Monitor collects and analyzes operational telemetry. They answer different operational questions.

cells.question: What improvements does Microsoft recommend for my deployed resources?
Is an Azure platform incident, maintenance event, or advisory affecting what I use?
What do my resources and applications' telemetry show right now and over time?

reveal.text: Advisor recommends improvements. Service Health reports Azure platform health relevant to you. Azure Monitor observes telemetry from workloads and resources.
Recommendation → Advisor. Azure outage or planned maintenance → Service Health. Metrics, logs, app telemetry, or alerts → Azure Monitor.
